entries.name: tether_boot_generate
entries.description: Generate a boot prompt for an agent by profile ID. The boot prompt assembles slot content from static files, role summaries, skill indexes, shell commands, and HTTP endpoints as defined in the profile YAML. Pipe the output to a CLI tool or capture it for an API provider.

entries.name: tether_catalog_apply
entries.description: Install a catalog plan the operator has approved. Refused unless the plan is approved, unexpired and the live catalog still matches what was reviewed. Backs up the whole catalog first, installs file by file, restores the touched files if anything fails or the catalog no longer validates, and returns the backup id, the files changed and an audit note to post on the Torque task. activation=restart_required means the daemon still runs the old definitions until it is restarted; that restart is a separate step the operator approves. Requires the catalog.write scope.

entries.name: tether_catalog_backups
entries.description: List catalog backups, newest first. Each is the whole catalog as it was before an apply; pass its id as rollback_of to tether_catalog_plan. Read-only; no scope required.

entries.name: tether_catalog_files
entries.description: List the catalog files you can read raw, or read one with path. Use it to fetch the current content of an agent, launch, project, skill, boot profile or team definition before editing it, then send the whole edited file to tether_catalog_plan. Reading a team-definitions/ file also returns its pin (id, revision, digest) for the definition pins in teams-policy.yaml. Providers, MCP servers, sandbox profiles and global.yaml are not readable (they hold credentials or daemon policy), and a file that contains an obvious secret is refused. Read-only; no scope required.

entries.name: tether_catalog_history
entries.description: List applied catalog changes, newest first: when, the plan name and task, the files changed, who planned it (principal, session, agent), when it was approved, the privileged changes, and the backup id that undoes it (pass it as rollback_of to tether_catalog_plan). Read-only; no scope required.

entries.name: tether_catalog_list_agents
entries.description: List all agent profiles defined in the tether catalog.

entries.name: tether_catalog_list_boot_profiles
entries.description: List available boot prompt profiles from the catalog boot-profiles directory.

entries.name: tether_catalog_list_launches
entries.description: List all launch profiles in the tether catalog. A launch profile combines a project, agent, and provider into a named runnable configuration.

entries.name: tether_catalog_list_projects
entries.description: List all projects defined in the tether catalog.

entries.name: tether_catalog_list_providers
entries.description: List all provider definitions in the tether catalog.

entries.name: tether_catalog_plan
entries.description: Review a catalog change without applying it. Send a bundle of whole files (create, replace or delete) under the catalog root, or rollback_of to restore a backup. The daemon checks every path against an allowlist (agents, launches, projects, providers, skills, boot-profiles, mcp-servers, sandbox-profiles, team-definitions, global.yaml, teams-policy.yaml; never credentials/), refuses obvious secrets, applies the bundle to a scratch copy, validates it and returns a diff, the digest, which changes are privileged (permissions, network, scopes, daemon defaults) and which running sessions use the touched definitions. Nothing live changes. You cannot change your own agent or launch definition. A plan is installed only after the operator approves it by digest at a terminal; ask them to run `tether catalog approve <plan_id>`. The plan expires at expires_at (ttl_seconds after creation, default 15 minutes); if it lapsed before approval, call tether_catalog_plan again with the same bundle and the same plan_id and digest are re-armed. Requires the catalog.write scope.

entries.name: tether_catalog_plan_get
entries.description: Read a catalog plan: its state (planned, invalid, approved, applied), digest, diff and validation. Read-only; no scope required.

entries.name: tether_catalog_refresh
entries.description: Refresh eligible upstream tool inventories in the shared daemon pool.

entries.name: tether_catalog_reload
entries.description: Make the daemon re-read its catalog from disk and use it for new launches, without a restart. The catalog is validated first; one that does not load or validate is refused and nothing changes. Agents, projects, providers, launches and sandbox profiles are swapped in. Running sessions keep what they started with. Settings in global.yaml that the daemon reads once at start (listener, identity, AI providers, MCP gateway, modules) are not swapped: the report lists them under restart_required. Returns what was added, removed and changed per kind. Requires the catalog.write scope.

entries.name: tether_catalog_validate
entries.description: Validate the catalog and return structured findings (severity, check, entity, message, remedy), failures first. With no files it checks the LIVE catalog. With files it checks what the catalog would be with that bundle applied, on a scratch copy; nothing is stored or written, so use it to test a draft before tether_catalog_plan. Checks: the layered load and parse, MCP grants against the declared servers, references between agents, launches, projects and providers, sandbox profiles, MCP discovery modes, profiles, server names and credential files. It reads files only; it does not contact a daemon, a database or an upstream. Read-only; no scope required.

entries.name: tether_channel_list
entries.description: List named channels with derived addresses; no membership is required.

entries.name: tether_channel_read
entries.description: Read durable channel history oldest first. Resume with next_since; purged messages carry tombstones. SSE subscriptions use HTTP.

entries.name: tether_docs_get
entries.description: Read one embedded MCP guide and its reference-file manifest. Use an id from tether_docs_list; fetch a declared reference with tether_docs_get_file.

entries.name: tether_docs_get_file
entries.description: Read one embedded reference file declared in a guide's manifest. Supply its guide id and exact manifest path; arbitrary host paths and URLs are not supported.

entries.name: tether_docs_list
entries.description: List the running Tether binary's MCP guides: titles and one-line usage triggers only. Choose an id, then use tether_docs_get for instructions and its reference-file manifest.

entries.name: tether_events_history
entries.description: Query durable daemon/session/broker event history from the shared events table. Returns newest first.

entries.name: tether_events_tool_calls
entries.description: Query recent proxied tool call events recorded by tether. Returns up to `limit` events (default 50, max 500), newest last. Available only in --proxy mode.

entries.name: tether_events_wait
entries.description: Wait briefly for live daemon or session events from the tetherd event stream. Useful for bounded polling-style MCP flows without maintaining a long-lived SSE connection.

entries.name: tether_execution_status
entries.description: Read the execution policy (global go/pause, environment session cap, per-project caps) and live session counts. Same as `tether execution status`. Read-only; needs the daemon. Launches over a cap or while paused are refused with execution_paused, environment_cap_reached or project_cap_reached.

entries.name: tether_forum_archive
entries.description: Archive board and block descendant writes.

entries.name: tether_forum_category_archive
entries.description: Archive category; descendant writes are blocked while reads remain available.

entries.name: tether_forum_category_create
entries.description: Create one category in a consumer namespace; no nested categories. Operator only.

entries.name: tether_forum_category_delete
entries.description: Delete an empty category; cascade=true explicitly deletes all contained boards and content. Operator only.

entries.name: tether_forum_category_get
entries.description: Read a visible category.

entries.name: tether_forum_category_list
entries.description: List visible categories with namespace and archive filters.

entries.name: tether_forum_category_unarchive
entries.description: Restore category; independently archived descendants stay archived.

entries.name: tether_forum_category_update
entries.description: Update category title or description. Operator only.

entries.name: tether_forum_clone
entries.description: Deep-copy board and content with new IDs. Supply new id; optional destination_category_id. Clone belongs to caller; participant grants are not copied.

entries.name: tether_forum_create
entries.description: Register a durable discussion forum as the operator. Namespace: app/<consumer>/forum/<instance>; multiple boards share a namespace. Optional category_id groups boards. Use forums for topics and threaded discussion, groups for chat, messages for delivery, and channels for event history.

entries.name: tether_forum_delete
entries.description: Delete an empty board; cascade=true explicitly deletes topics and posts.

entries.name: tether_forum_get
entries.description: Read a forum's configuration and policy, then discover topics with tether_forum_topic_list.

entries.name: tether_forum_list
entries.description: List accessible forums in compact pages; expand one with tether_forum_get.

entries.name: tether_forum_move
entries.description: Move board within its namespace to destination_category_id; empty string places it at root.

entries.name: tether_forum_owner_set
entries.description: Operator only: transfer forum ownership; omitted owner defaults to operator. Invite the old owner explicitly before transfer to retain access.

entries.name: tether_forum_participant_add
entries.description: Operator only: grant read or post (includes read) access to an authenticated stable principal, or update its grant.

entries.name: tether_forum_participant_list
entries.description: Operator only: list explicit stable-principal grants with bounded pagination.

entries.name: tether_forum_participant_revoke
entries.description: Operator only: revoke a grant; subsequent requests and cursor continuations recheck access. Owners retain implicit access.

entries.name: tether_forum_post_clone
entries.description: Copy a message and its replies to destination_topic_id with new IDs and source references; optional parent_post_id.

entries.name: tether_forum_post_create
entries.description: Write Markdown to a topic; parent_post_id creates a reply within that topic. Author and session provenance are stamped by the daemon.

entries.name: tether_forum_post_delete
entries.description: Delete a message; cascade=true is required to delete its reply subtree.

entries.name: tether_forum_post_get
entries.description: Open a selected post: detail=summary (160 characters), preview (2000), or full (up to 100000). Inspect truncated and body_chars.

entries.name: tether_forum_post_list
entries.description: Read compact post previews in sequence order. since_seq fetches newer posts; next_cursor continues a bounded page.

entries.name: tether_forum_post_move
entries.description: Move a message and its replies to destination_topic_id; optional parent_post_id reparents the subtree. IDs are retained.

entries.name: tether_forum_post_update
entries.description: Edit message body_md, subject or attachment references; original attribution is retained. Owner or operator.

entries.name: tether_forum_search
entries.description: Search topic titles and post bodies within one accessible forum. Returns compact matched posts; open selected results with tether_forum_post_get.

entries.name: tether_forum_topic_archive
entries.description: Archive thread without losing open/resolved status.

entries.name: tether_forum_topic_clone
entries.description: Copy entire thread to destination_forum_id with new IDs and source references.

entries.name: tether_forum_topic_create
entries.description: Create an open discussion topic in a forum. The daemon stamps the author; add the first post separately.

entries.name: tether_forum_topic_delete
entries.description: Delete an empty thread; cascade=true explicitly deletes its posts.

entries.name: tether_forum_topic_fork
entries.description: Copy post_id and its replies from topic_id into a new thread in destination_forum_id. Source is retained.

entries.name: tether_forum_topic_get
entries.description: Read topic metadata and a paginated post outline (ids, authors, depth, short previews). Open selected bodies with tether_forum_post_get.

entries.name: tether_forum_topic_list
entries.description: List compact topic rows with status, author, date and provenance filters. Resume with next_cursor.

entries.name: tether_forum_topic_move
entries.description: Move entire thread to destination_forum_id within its namespace, retaining IDs and attribution.

entries.name: tether_forum_topic_unarchive
entries.description: Restore thread and its previous open/resolved status.

entries.name: tether_forum_topic_update
entries.description: Update thread title or open/resolved status. Owner or operator.

entries.name: tether_forum_unarchive
entries.description: Restore board; independently archived topics stay archived.

entries.name: tether_forum_update
entries.description: Update board title, description, config and metadata. Owner or operator.

entries.name: tether_group_archive
entries.description: Soft-delete a group (sets status='archived'). The group becomes read-only — members can still read history, but no new messages are accepted. Only the owner or a moderator can archive. Requires the groups.write scope.

entries.name: tether_group_create
entries.description: Create a new group (federation directory kind=group). The server mints the URN — 3-segment msg://group/<authority>/grp_<10alnum>. The creator is automatically added to the group with role='owner'. The display_name is required; description, role (group category), and capabilities (topic tags) are optional. The creator URN is supplied via 'creator_urn' (auth surrogate for v060-05; v060-03 token auth will replace). Requires the groups.write scope.

entries.name: tether_group_invite
entries.description: Add a member to a group. Only owners and moderators can invite. The member URN must exist in the registry. Role defaults to 'member' if unset. Requires the groups.write scope.

entries.name: tether_group_kick
entries.description: Remove a member from a group. Only owners and moderators can kick. The group's owner cannot be removed by this tool — the owner must use tether_group_leave after transferring ownership via tether_group_set_role. Requires the groups.write scope.

entries.name: tether_group_leave
entries.description: Self-remove from a group. If the leaver is the group's owner, another member must already hold owner or moderator role — otherwise the leave is refused with cannot_leave_without_owner_transfer (forbidden). Use tether_group_set_role to promote first. Requires the groups.write scope.

entries.name: tether_group_list_for_member
entries.description: List the groups a member belongs to. Returns active + archived groups (archived ones are still visible to former members). Read-only.

entries.name: tether_group_list_members
entries.description: List the members of a group, ordered by joined_at. Display names are hydrated from the registry. Read-only.

entries.name: tether_group_lookup
entries.description: Look up a group by URN. Returns the full Profile. The 'urn' must be a group URN (msg://group/...); agent URNs return not_found. Archived groups are still returned (callers may need their metadata). Read-only.

entries.name: tether_group_mark_read
entries.description: Bump the caller's read cursor for a group. Idempotent / monotonic — smaller up_to_seq is silently a no-op. Requires the groups.write scope.

entries.name: tether_group_mentions
entries.description: List the caller's own mention notices across all groups. Filters by timestamp (since) and limit. Read-only.

entries.name: tether_group_post
entries.description:
Post a message to a group. The caller (from_urn) must be a member; the group must not be archived. Returns {message_id, group_seq}. 

SYMBOL VOCABULARY (v060-05 D6 — important):
  - '@<urn>' or '@<display_name>' = MENTION. The daemon parses the body before commit, resolves each token via the registry, and emits a notice envelope to the mentioned URN's personal inbox after the group message commits. Short-form ('@<display_name>') resolves via registry Lookup; ambiguous (two members share the same display_name) returns invalid_request with a 'candidates' list — re-issue with the full URN.
  - '!<command> [args...]' = ACTION/COMMAND. RESERVED NAMESPACE — the daemon does NOT parse '!'. The transport delivers '!' bytes verbatim; consuming agents decide what '!deploy --branch=main' means in their command handler. Reserved so future tooling (linters, audit log filters) can rely on the convention.
  - ':<directive> <prompt>' = DIRECTIVE. RESERVED NAMESPACE — the daemon does NOT parse ':'. The consuming agent routes the directive through whatever directives-package implementation it has installed locally. The actual directive vocabulary, security model, and dispatch mechanics are owned by the directives package, not this sprint.
  - To send any of these symbols literally, escape with '\@', '\!', or '\:' — the daemon never resolves an escaped form. Useful for documentation, examples, and quoted snippets.

Requires the groups.write scope.

entries.name: tether_group_read
entries.description: Non-destructive read of group messages. Does NOT bump the read cursor — call tether_group_mark_read after acknowledging the batch. Default since_seq is the caller's last_read_seq (0 → from cursor). thread_id filters to one sub-conversation. Read-only.

entries.name: tether_group_set_role
entries.description: Change a member's role within a group. Promotion to 'owner' is owner-only (transfers ownership). Moderators can promote to 'moderator' but not to 'owner'. Requires the groups.write scope.

entries.name: tether_health
entries.description: Health check for the tether MCP adapter. Returns version and catalog summary.

entries.name: tether_logical_agent_list
entries.description: List all logical agents registered in the tether store. Logical agents are durable identities that persist across sessions and accumulate checkpoints.

entries.name: tether_logical_agent_resume
entries.description: Resume a logical agent: starts a new session using its most recent checkpoint as the boot context. Requires session.write scope.

entries.name: tether_message_archive
entries.description: Archive (soft-delete) a message for its recipient (idempotent). Archived messages drop out of default tether_message_list results. Requires message.write scope.

entries.name: tether_message_cancel
entries.description: Cancel a pending message. Requires message.write scope.

entries.name: tether_message_consume
entries.description: Mark a message as consumed by the recipient. Requires message.write scope.

entries.name: tether_message_get
entries.description: Get a message envelope by ID.

entries.name: tether_message_inbox
entries.description: Pull a recipient's undelivered messages (atomic-delivery agent pull model). DESTRUCTIVE: returned messages are marked delivered and will not appear in a future inbox call; when the calling session is the recipient itself, they are also marked consumed. For a non-destructive, repeatable listing use tether_message_list instead.

entries.name: tether_message_interrupt
entries.description: Interrupt the running turn of the session that sent a routed message and deliver body as its next turn (reply with interrupt:true). Fails with interrupt_unsupported when the runtime cannot cancel a turn. Requires message.write scope.

entries.name: tether_message_list
entries.description: List a recipient's messages non-destructively. Repeatable: no delivered_at/read_at side effects. Each message carries read_at/archived_at state and a subject/body payload projection. Archived messages are excluded unless include_archived is set.

entries.name: tether_message_mark_read
entries.description: Mark a message as read by its recipient (idempotent). Does not consume or delete it. Requires message.write scope.

entries.name: tether_message_notify
entries.description: Send a message envelope and best-effort wake a live recipient session with a mailbox notification turn. Requires message.write scope.

entries.name: tether_message_purge
entries.description: Clear one message's body/metadata, leaving its structural/trace fields (id, kind, from, to, thread, timestamps) intact. Irreversible. Refuses with an error when the message has a pending delivery obligation -- including dead-lettered, which remains repairable via tether_message_redrive and would resend an empty message if purged first. Idempotent: purging an already-purged message reports purged=false, not an error. Requires the delivery.write scope.

entries.name: tether_message_redrive
entries.description: Authorized retry of a dead-lettered delivery. Idempotent: calling this again on an already-retryable delivery reports redriven=false, not an error. message_id may be a literal delivery id to address one specific group-fanout recipient's delivery (use tether_message_trace or an operator's own inspection to find it). Requires the delivery.write scope.

entries.name: tether_message_reply
entries.description: Reply to the session that sent a routed message (one a session published to a channel); the body is delivered as that session's next turn at its next idle boundary. Same route as POST /messages/{id}/reply. Requires message.write scope. For an ordinary mailbox message (from a user, device or agent address) this fails with reply_target_not_a_session: answer it with tether_message_send to its sender and in_reply_to=<message_id>.

entries.name: tether_message_retention_candidates
entries.description: Preview messages eligible for a body purge -- read-only, mutates nothing. Use this before tether_message_purge to check a message's eligibility (a pending, leased, retry_scheduled or dead-lettered delivery is never eligible; see tether_message_purge's description for why dead-lettered is excluded). No scope required.

entries.name: tether_message_send
entries.description: Send a message envelope via the tether messaging store. Requires message.write scope.

entries.name: tether_message_thread
entries.description: List all messages in a thread by thread ID, scoped to the ones involving the claimed identity.

entries.name: tether_message_trace
entries.description: Show the structured delivery trace for a message: who sent to whom, why a binding resolved, which host accepted, which turn was submitted, and why retry/expiry occurred. Read-only; no scope required.

entries.name: tether_message_unarchive
entries.description: Restore an archived message for its recipient (idempotent). Requires message.write scope.

entries.name: tether_proxy_events
entries.description: Query durable proxy/tool call events from the SQLite store. Supports filtering by session, server, tool, errors-only, and since cursor.

entries.name: tether_registry_binding_current
entries.description: Get the authoritative current binding for a target -- the highest-generation, non-revoked, non-expired binding. Read-only; no scope required.

entries.name: tether_registry_binding_lease
entries.description: Lease a published-local (pull-only) RuntimeBinding for a target URN -- the external bridge registration surface T07 defines. Always mints visibility='published-local'; capabilities must be exactly ["pull-only"]. Refuses (conflict) to supersede a binding Tether itself manages (private-local/tether-hosted). Requires the registry.write scope.

entries.name: tether_registry_binding_list
entries.description: List every binding ever leased for a target, newest generation first (audit view). Read-only; no scope required.

entries.name: tether_registry_binding_renew
entries.description: Extend an existing binding's lease. Fails (conflict) if a newer generation now exists for the same target. Requires the registry.write scope.

entries.name: tether_registry_binding_revoke
entries.description: Relinquish a binding lease. Idempotent. Requires the registry.write scope.

entries.name: tether_registry_deregister
entries.description: Soft-delete a registry row. Status flips to 'deprecated'. The row remains visible via direct URN lookup (so callers can audit deprecated entries); default Search excludes it. Returns the deprecated Profile. Requires the registry.write scope.

entries.name: tether_registry_lookup
entries.description: Look up a registry profile by URN. Returns the redacted Profile by default or not_found. Soft-deleted (status='deprecated') rows are returned by direct lookup — they are excluded only from default Search results. Read-only by default; passing sensitive operational fields ('callback', 'kind_meta', 'host_address', 'all') in include requires the registry.write scope, while correlation identifiers ('external_ids') are accessible with read scope.

entries.name: tether_registry_lookup_by
entries.description: Resolve a substrate-local external ID to one registry profile. Returns 0 or 1 row; use this when you know a local ID like a Tether catalog slug, Torque project ID, or Cerberus owner and want the canonical registry URN. Read-only; passing sensitive operational fields in include requires registry.write scope, while correlation identifiers ('external_ids') are accessible with read scope.

entries.name: tether_registry_merge
entries.description: Merge a source profile into a destination profile: the source's external-ID mappings are reattached to the destination and the source row is soft-deleted (status='deprecated'). Returns the canonical destination Profile. Requires the registry.write scope.

entries.name: tether_registry_register
entries.description: Register a new agent or project profile in the federation directory. Server mints the URN (Stripe-style opaque id, e.g. agt_xxxxxxxxxx / prj_xxxxxxxxxx); callers MUST NOT supply the urn field — doing so returns invalid_request. The kind argument selects the entity kind. The profile argument is a JSON object matching registry.Profile: required fields are display_name; optional fields include title, role, description, avatar, project, status, callback, capabilities, skills (each {name, learned_at RFC3339, optional via, level}), links (each {kind, target}), kind_meta, host_address, health_status. Returns the canonical Profile with the minted URN. Requires the registry.write scope.

entries.name: tether_registry_scoped_binding_resolve
entries.description: Resolve the current revision for (scope, slot). single=true resolves to exactly one target, erroring (conflict) on zero or multiple targets rather than making the caller guess. Read-only; no scope required.

entries.name: tether_registry_scoped_binding_revisions
entries.description: List every revision ever published for (scope, slot), newest first. Read-only; no scope required.

entries.name: tether_registry_scoped_binding_set
entries.description: Publish a new revision for a consumer-owned (scope, slot) role binding, e.g. scope='run-42' slot='reviewer'. Tether does not interpret scope/slot names or grant command authority from a binding. Requires the registry.write scope.

entries.name: tether_registry_search
entries.description: Search the registry by filter. All filters combine with AND. Result ordering is alphabetical on display_name. Default excludes status='deprecated'; pass status='deprecated' to return only deprecated rows, or status='*' to return all statuses. Read-only; no scope required.

entries.name: tether_registry_sync
entries.description:
Refresh thin-profile columns from the row's callback URI. Returns one of two success shapes:
  - {ok:true, synced:false} when the row has no callback configured (no-op state).
  - {ok:true, synced:true, profile:<refreshed>} when the callback was invoked successfully.
Raw payload is NEVER stored (substrate ops-store files often contain plaintext secrets); only the thin-profile columns + capabilities/skills/links arrays + cached_at are updated. Requires the registry.write scope.

entries.name: tether_registry_update_self
entries.description:
Partial-merge update of a registry row. Returns the refreshed Profile. Scalar fields (display_name, title, role, description, avatar, project, status, health_status, host_address, last_seen_at, kind_meta, guidelines) update column-wise — only fields present in the patch are touched. Array fields (capabilities, skills, links, tags, entry_points) accept TWO wire shapes:
  (1) Shorthand `[...]` — equivalent to {mode:'replace', value:[...]}.
  (2) Explicit `{mode: 'replace'|'append'|'remove', value: [...]}`.
Empty value is always a no-op (existing arrays are not cleared). Remove matches: capabilities, tags, and entry_points by string equality; skills by name; links by (kind, target) tuple. last_updated_by is required on every patch — caller-supplied identity string, becomes auth-bound in v060-02. Requires the registry.write scope.

entries.name: tether_routing_get
entries.description: Get installed routing capabilities for the gateway or a session. Per-output final-text confidence is authoritative.

entries.name: tether_session_attachments
entries.description: List client attach/detach records for a session.

entries.name: tether_session_checkpoints
entries.description: List checkpoints for a session (via its logical agent). Returns newest first.

entries.name: tether_session_create
entries.description: Create a session from a launch profile (state=created, not yet running). Follow with tether_session_launch to start it. Supports v005-08 Agent Ops Tier-2 caller-provided payloads (agent_file / agent_inline / boot_profile / override / prompt_append) — when any are set, they merge over the catalog-resolved agent + boot profile.

entries.name: tether_session_events
entries.description: List historical lifecycle events for a session. Returns events in descending seq order (newest first).

entries.name: tether_session_get
entries.description: Get a single agent session by ID.

entries.name: tether_session_health
entries.description: Get the live runtime health snapshot for a running session. Returns provider identity, capability flags, live state, and observed last_activity_at, pending_approval and pending_question when known. Omitted observations are unknown, not false. Returns not_found if the session does not exist, conflict if the session is not currently running.

entries.name: tether_session_launch
entries.description: Start a previously created session (transitions from created → running). Returns launch details including workspace path and log path.

entries.name: tether_session_list
entries.description: List agent sessions. Optionally filter by state (created, ready, launching, running, detached, orphaned, completed, failed, killed) and paginate with cursor and limit.

entries.name: tether_session_peek
entries.description: Digest of a session's recent stream-json output: state, init, tool calls, results and the FINAL line, with secrets redacted. Same digest as `tether sessions peek`. Read-only; needs the daemon.

entries.name: tether_session_refs
entries.description:
List what a session touched, or -- with workstream_id instead -- everything every session in a workstream touched. The workstream form is the one that survives a compaction, since a compaction creates a new session row.

Reading `source`: session/operator identifies the verified credential that wrote the ref. proxy means hub-observed traffic, not truth; arguments remain agent-authored. Historical proxy_claimed is untrusted. api is unattributed capture and agent is a legacy assertion. None validates the identifier. Absence is not evidence: direct MCP children, HTTP callers and the CLI can bypass capture.

entries.name: tether_session_resize
entries.description: Resize the PTY terminal for a running session.

entries.name: tether_session_send_input
entries.description: Send raw text input to a running session's stdin (PTY). Use to interact with a CLI agent session.

entries.name: tether_session_send_turn
entries.description: Send a user turn to a running session with lifecycle-aware framing. Streaming-stdio sessions (Claude mode-5) receive an NDJSON user-message envelope; jsonrpc-stdio sessions (Codex app-server) get initialize+thread/start lazily followed by turn/start; PTY and unknown modes fall back to raw stdin. Prefer this over tether_session_send_input for long-lived agent turns — it removes per-call framing burden. A provider_session_lost error means the provider no longer has the session's resume id: the turn was not delivered, and resending starts a fresh provider session without the old history.

entries.name: tether_session_stop
entries.description: Send a stop signal to a running session.

entries.name: tether_session_wait
entries.description: Block until the session exits and return its exit code plus the final turn result (stop_reason, output_text) when one was recorded. Use after tether_session_stop or for short-lived sessions.

entries.name: tether_skill_broker
entries.description: Return ranked skill recommendations for a specific task, role, project, or trigger set. This is the progressive-discovery companion to tether_skill_list: it returns metadata, reasons, and ranking, then the caller uses tether_skill_get for the chosen skill body.

entries.name: tether_skill_get
entries.description: Load a Tether skill by id and return its instructions. Use when a boot prompt lists a skill pointer like `/refactor-go`; pass `refactor-go` as skill_id, then follow the returned body.

entries.name: tether_skill_list
entries.description: List Tether skills visible through layered discovery. Returns id, name, description, triggers, path, and layer; use tether_skill_get to load a skill body.

entries.name: tether_team_address
entries.description: Team address through the authenticated daemon service. Requires a caller-scoped idempotency key; retries retain the original result. No asserted caller identity is accepted.

entries.name: tether_team_adopt
entries.description: Team adopt through the authenticated daemon service. Requires a caller-scoped idempotency key; retries retain the original result. No asserted caller identity is accepted.

entries.name: tether_team_assign
entries.description: Team assign through the authenticated daemon service. Requires a caller-scoped idempotency key; retries retain the original result. No asserted caller identity is accepted.

entries.name: tether_team_cancel
entries.description: Team cancel through the authenticated daemon service. Requires a caller-scoped idempotency key; retries retain the original result. No asserted caller identity is accepted.

entries.name: tether_team_delegate
entries.description: Team delegate through the authenticated daemon service. Requires a caller-scoped idempotency key; retries retain the original result. No asserted caller identity is accepted.

entries.name: tether_team_dissolve
entries.description: Team dissolve through the authenticated daemon service. Requires a caller-scoped idempotency key; retries retain the original result. No asserted caller identity is accepted.

entries.name: tether_team_form
entries.description: Team form through the authenticated daemon service. Requires a caller-scoped idempotency key; retries retain the original result. No asserted caller identity is accepted. request.team is a versioned definition with id, name, version, slots, phases, authority, routing and policy; coordinator/member roster shortcuts are not supported. Stage A uses coordinator/workers/reviewer slots and operator-approved definition pins.

entries.name: tether_team_member_add
entries.description: Team member_add through the authenticated daemon service. Requires a caller-scoped idempotency key; retries retain the original result. No asserted caller identity is accepted.

entries.name: tether_team_member_remove
entries.description: Team member_remove through the authenticated daemon service. Requires a caller-scoped idempotency key; retries retain the original result. No asserted caller identity is accepted.

entries.name: tether_team_report_result
entries.description: Team report_result through the authenticated daemon service. Requires a caller-scoped idempotency key; retries retain the original result. No asserted caller identity is accepted.

entries.name: tether_tool_metrics
entries.description: Read counters and cumulative latency histograms for completed tool calls (including rejected calls) from retained durable events. Groups by exact tool, upstream and outcome (and optionally discovery mode); bounded to 1000 groups with an explicit truncated flag. Use compact=true for a small summary. No argument values or identity labels.

entries.name: tether_whoami
entries.description: Self-discovery: the registered Profile (if any), attached external-id mappings, group memberships, and the current RuntimeBinding (host/session currently owning delivery), if any, for the claimed URN. An unregistered or never-bound identity is not an error -- every field is independently best-effort.

entries.name: tether_workstream_assign
entries.description: Assign a session to a workstream, or clear it by passing an empty workstream_id. Requires the session.write scope.

entries.name: tether_workstream_attach
entries.description: Record that a session touched an object: a Torque task, a git commit or PR, a Tesseract revision, a Cerberus deploy, an ADR, a URL. Idempotent -- re-attaching the same (kind, ref_id, relation) is a no-op, not an error, so a hook that runs twice is safe. A repeat does NOT revise the original: the row records what was asserted at the time. Refs attach to the session and roll up through its workstream, so they survive a compaction. Requires the session.write scope.

entries.name: tether_workstream_create
entries.description: Create a workstream: the durable container for work that outlives any one session. A resume/compact/fork child inherits its parent's workstream automatically, so a container attached here survives a compaction, which creates a new session row and orphans anything keyed on session_id. Requires the session.write scope.

entries.name: tether_workstream_digest
entries.description:
What a session, or a whole workstream across its lineage, actually touched and actually left behind. This is the recovery view: hand the output to an agent as context rather than reading a transcript.

Pass session_id for the everyday grain (what did I touch this session) or workstream_id for the roll-up across a compaction. Exactly one.

Refs are split into left_behind (created/updated -- what this work produced) and touched (read/referenced -- what it consulted). Read left_behind first; it is what a reviewer and a recovery instruction both care about.

BEFORE CONCLUDING A SESSION DID NOTHING, read coverage. Every session in the span carries a ref_attribution saying whether its proxy could produce an observed ref at all, and coverage.proxy_attributable counts how many could. When that is zero, an empty source=proxy column is a fact about configuration and says nothing about what the agent did. coverage.truncated says whether the ref list was cut at the limit.

entries.name: tether_workstream_ensure
entries.description: Return the workstream containing a session, creating one for the whole lineage when it has none. This is the one-call path for a session that needs a container without ceremony. Idempotent: a second call returns the same workstream. Requires the session.write scope.

entries.name: tether_workstream_get
entries.description: Fetch one workstream by id.

entries.name: tether_workstream_list
entries.description: List one bounded workstream page, newest first. Follow next_cursor with unchanged filters; complete is live exhaustion, not a snapshot.

entries.name: tether_workstream_namespace
entries.description:
Resolve where a session's workstream-scoped scratch belongs in Tesseract workspace. Write the content to Tesseract yourself (with workstream_id as an attribute) and attach the returned item or revision id with tether_workstream_attach — Tether stores the location and references, never the content.

Workstream ID is an attribute, never a namespace path segment. Material lives in Tesseract's workspace domain: project-owned scratch under project/<project-id>/workspace/scratch or Tether's cross-project scratch under app/tether/workspace/scratch.

entries.name: tether_workstream_update
entries.description: Partially update an existing workstream by id. Only the fields you pass change: omit a field to leave it alone, pass an empty string for name or workflow_id to clear it. status must be active or closed. id and created_at are immutable; updated_at is set. Returns the refreshed workstream. Requires the session.write scope.

entries.name: tether_workstreams_for_ref
entries.description:
Which workstreams contain a session that touched this object -- the reverse lookup. Use it when you hold an identifier and want the work it came out of: "which Tesseract records came from CW-20260911-0039?" starts here, then digests the result.

RETURNS A PAGE OF MATCHES; FOLLOW next_cursor UNTIL complete. Two separate efforts touching the same task is ordinary, so a single answer would look authoritative and be wrong whenever the ambiguity is real.

entries.name: todo_update
entries.description:
Update a todo's title, description, status, priority, labels, or metadata. Omitted or null fields stay unchanged. An empty string clears the field, except status and priority, where an empty string is invalid. Labels must be a JSON array encoded as a string; a labels array argument is rejected.

**When to use:** When the user marks a task done, blocks it, changes its priority, or renames it. Typical status transitions: pending → in_progress → done, or → blocked.

**Required context:** You need the todo ID. Get it from todo_list if you don't have it.

**Output shape:** Updated todo JSON on success.

entries.name: tool_describe
entries.description:
Return a tool's contract on demand: description, input schema, golden examples, and related tools/skills.

**When to use:** When you're unsure about a tool's input shape, when you've never rendered a particular envelope `type` for `card_show`, or after a call fails with a schema-validation error. Cheap (registry + embed lookup, no LLM call) — prefer it to failing-and-retrying.

**Catalog:** Describes built-in and connected MCP tools from the same registry as tool_list. This is schema discovery, not a permission grant; use request_tools to load a tool for this turn.

**Output shape:** {name, description, input_schema, examples: [{title, args, result?, notes?}], related_tools?: [string], related_skills?: [string]}.

**Unknown tool name:** Returns a structured error with `closest_matches` (Levenshtein) so you can correct typos in one round-trip.

entries.name: tool_list
entries.description:
Lists registered built-in and connected MCP tools by name and one-line summary. Returns the full inventory regardless of caller — actual reachability for any specific tool is governed by agent permissions and project/session policy, not by this output.

**Contract:** input `{filter?: string}` (optional case-insensitive substring matched against BOTH name and summary). Output `{tools: [{name, summary}], count}`.

**When to use:** Browse the catalog when you're not sure which tool to reach for, or confirm a tool name exists before calling it. Use `tool_describe` next for the full schema of a specific tool, and `request_tools` to load a tool for use in the current turn.

**Example:** `tool_list({filter:"schedule_create"}) → {tools:[{name:"schedule_create", summary:"Create an agent schedule."}], count:1}`.

**See also:** `tool_describe(name="<tool>")` for the full contract (schema, golden examples, related tools) of any single tool returned here.

entries.name: tool_validate
entries.description:
Pre-flight check: validate a proposed tool-call's arguments against the tool's declared input schema, without invoking the tool. Cheap, deterministic, no side effects.

**When to use:** Pre-flight check before high-blast-radius calls (envelope emission, mutations, network-effecting tools) when you're unsure whether your `args` shape will be accepted. Cheap, deterministic, side-effect-free.

**When NOT to use:** Don't call this on every tool invocation reflexively — only when the schema is unfamiliar or the call is expensive. Pure read-only tools (search, list, get) typically don't justify a pre-flight; just call them and read the error if they reject the input.

**Output shape:** `{valid: bool, errors: [{path, reason, suggestion?}]}` where `path` is a JSON Pointer rooted at the args object (e.g. `/data/metrics/0/label`), `reason` is the leaf schema-violation message, and `suggestion` (when present) is a single-step fix hint such as `"add required field 'metrics'"` or `"wrap in `[...]`"`. On `valid: true`, errors is `[]`.

**Special case:** `card_show` validates `args.data` against the per-type envelope schema in addition to the top-level input schema, so the agent gets per-field feedback against the schema that actually rejects bad payloads (the top-level schema only declares `data: object`).

Response shape: data = <Envelope> for the response (kind=response, in_reply_to=<request id>).
Example: {"from":"msg://agent/test/alice","to":"msg://agent/test/bob","payload":"{\"q\":\"ping\"}","timeout_seconds":"15"}

entries.name: torque_inbox_poll
entries.description:
Opt into mid-session inbox polling AND drain your inbox in one call (CW-20260518-0042).
By default Torque delivers envelopes addressed to a live agent by injecting them as the agent's next turn (inject-at-turn-boundary). An agent that is actively communicating can instead PULL its own inbox between tool calls: each torque_inbox_poll call records a polling opt-in for the 'to' URN, and while that opt-in is fresh the steering bridge stops injecting turns for that recipient — so a steering message is handled exactly once, by your poll.
The opt-in is time-bounded: it lapses after poll_ttl_seconds (returned in the response) unless you poll again. Keep polling on a cadence shorter than the TTL to stay opted in; stop polling (or pass release=true) to revert to inject-at-turn. 'to' MUST be your own address and match how senders address you (e.g. msg://agent/<authority>/<your-task-id>).
Response shape: data = {to, polling, poll_ttl_seconds, count, envelopes:[<Envelope>...], drain_hint?}.
